reuse.why: Creates a new getExpectedScheduleAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount, which already resolves missing/number/range amounts and is used across the UI, instead of changing that helper.

duplication.why: The new helper duplicates getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch, and the midpoint copies in forecast-schedules.ts and budget/schedule-template.ts are left alongside it.

placement.why: The new helper sits in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount, where the amount rule belongs.

scope.why: Only the three server/shared call sites, the helper and its tests.

maintainability.why: Two exported helpers now answer the same question with different rules (midpoint vs furthest from zero), and other copies still use the midpoint, so the rule depends on the caller.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount is added instead of updating getScheduledAmount (used by SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedules); forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts keep their own midpoint

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount re-creates getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range resolution under a new name

one_place.where: new rule only in getExpectedScheduleAmount (used by schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions); getScheduledAmount, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts still use the midpoint
